distinction_from_proof_packets.proof_packets: Primarily test a single doctrine or proposition
distinction_from_proof_packets.living_community_laboratories: Test how multiple doctrines interact within one real community

case_study_vs_pilot.pilot: Tries to prove the framework works
case_study_vs_pilot.comprehensive_community_case_study: Tries to understand how the framework would interact with a real community
case_study_vs_pilot.rule: Use case studies first. Do not brand early community work as pilots that validate Constitutional Capitalism.

investigator_alignment.purpose: Learn from the community — not demonstrate that the framework is already correct
investigator_alignment.success_includes: Finding that parts of the architecture need refinement

standard_case_structure.title: Community Baseline
standard_case_structure.purpose: Document current reality before any Constitutional Capitalism analysis

standard_case_structure.title: Opportunity Analysis
standard_case_structure.ask: Where does this community already have leverage?
standard_case_structure.not_ask: How do we implement Constitutional Capitalism?
standard_case_structure.rule: Analyze opportunities and tradeoffs rather than assume any particular outcome

standard_case_structure.title: Systems Mapping
standard_case_structure.purpose: Map interactions across community systems — whole-system picture, not single-industry analysis

standard_case_structure.title: Scenario Analysis
standard_case_structure.rule: Compare several plausible futures against the same metrics — not one preferred recommendation

standard_case_structure.title: Lessons
standard_case_structure.ask: What did this case teach us about the framework?
feeds: Which interactions were stronger than expected?

cases.title: Lewisville — First Comprehensive Community Case Study

working_rationale.note: User-identified case dimensions for investigation — not verified baseline facts. All baseline claims require registered sources before use.
why_interesting_as_research_site: Stable local leadership structure (multi-term mayor) — to be verified
Deep public-service / military leadership experience — to be verified
Direct exposure to a major economic transition (lithium development) — to be verified and scoped
Community scale small enough for systems-level understanding vs statewide averages — to be measured
working_rationale.research_value: More valuable than choosing a city merely because it is already successful — presents a real environment where multiple CC parts can be examined together

opportunity_focus_candidates: How lithium (or other resource) development could influence workforce, local ownership, housing, infrastructure, environmental stewardship, EMS, education, retirement/community wealth, entrepreneurship, and fiscal resilience — as research questions, not assumed outcomes
research_questions: Under what conditions does resource development produce durable local wealth?
How can communities retain more long-term value from resource extraction?
What institutions are needed to translate economic growth into broader prosperity?
What risks should be anticipated and mitigated?
honesty_rules: Do not invent Lewisville statistics, leadership claims, or lithium outcomes
Do not treat this as a pilot proving Constitutional Capitalism
Do not begin Parts I–VI until PP-FF-01 methodology rhythm is underway or parallel with clear priority: proof packets remain highest leverage
Baseline must use registered sources only

cases.title: Rose Bud Rural Education and Farm Community Laboratory

complements.lewisville_pathway: resource development, local ownership, infrastructure, community wealth
complements.rose_bud_pathway: rural education, agriculture, workforce preparation, population attraction, long-term community renewal

cases.central_research_question: Can a rural public school district become a regional education, agriculture, and skilled-trades hub that attracts students, strengthens the local economy, supports family farms, and creates a sustainable pathway for community growth?

working_concept.note: Unproven design agenda for research — not a claim of feasibility or funding.
working_concept.housing: graduated stages only after demonstrated demand and capacity

first_research_gate.title: Student funding / enrollment economics
first_research_gate.critical_calculation: Marginal recurring revenue per additional student minus full marginal cost of instruction, transportation, housing, food, staffing, student services, facilities, and compliance

arkansas_learns.rule: Do not assume Arkansas LEARNS automatically authorizes or funds the model. Tie each element to actual statutory or regulatory authority.

cases.funding_map_rule: USDA and other programs are potential tools, not presumed sources. Record eligibility, allowable use, match, renewal, timing, operations vs capital.
scenarios: Residential rural innovation center (housing only after earlier sustainability)
cases.proper_status_statement: Rose Bud Rural Education and Farm Community Laboratory — architecture scaffold only; statutory authority, enrollment economics, funding eligibility, community demand, and implementation feasibility remain unproven.
honesty_rules: Do not invent Rose Bud enrollment, finance, LEARNS, or USDA conclusions
Do not treat as pilot or claim existing funding will support the concept
Baseline and legal claims require registered sources only

priority_relative_to_proof_packets.rule: Living Community Laboratories are a research category. PP-FF-01 and proof-packet methodology remain the immediate execution priority. Case scaffolds may be captured now; deep baseline work should not displace proof packets.

paired_pathways.rule: Lewisville and Rose Bud are complementary Living Community Laboratories testing different prosperity pathways — resource/community wealth vs education/agriculture/renewal.

research_streams.title: Living Community Laboratory: Rural Prosperity Campus Model
research_streams.central_hypothesis: Can a rural public education system become the coordinating institution for rebuilding a regional food economy while simultaneously improving education, workforce development, family farm profitability, and community prosperity?
defining_questions: Can education itself become productive economic infrastructure?
Can a rural school district function as the coordinating institution for regional economic development without compromising its primary educational mission?
layers: Family Farm Network (partner, do not replace)
Natural Resource Partnerships (eligibility-aware; no presumed funding)
Food Security (local priorities + sustainable external markets)
empirical_questions: Does the model improve educational outcomes?
Does it strengthen family farm profitability?
Does it improve local food security?
Does it strengthen rather than weaken neighboring communities?
Under what conditions does it succeed or fail?

research_streams.title: Distributed Arkansas Prosperity Network (research concept)
research_streams.proposition: Regional living laboratories can specialize (e.g., Rose Bud — agriculture/food; Lewisville — resource development/community wealth; others — forestry, aquaculture, manufacturing, healthcare, transportation) while sharing curriculum, research, and operational lessons as a connected, non-identical statewide knowledge network.
research_streams.rule: Not centralized. Not identical. Connected. Each hub contributes unique specialty expertise.

comparative_methodology.rule: Lewisville and Rose Bud are not two independent curiosities — they begin a comparative research methodology across different engines of community development.
comparative_methodology.not_prescriptive: Constitutional Capitalism does not say every community should become Rose Bud (or Lewisville). It asks what engine of prosperity is most authentic to this community, and how institutions can help that engine create broad, durable local wealth.
comparative_methodology.guiding_question: What engine of prosperity is most authentic to this community, and how can institutions be designed to help that engine create broad, durable local wealth?

paired_engines.lewisville: How does a community translate emerging natural-resource opportunity into durable local prosperity?
paired_engines.rose_bud: How does a community translate education and human capital into durable local prosperity?

development_engines.question: How does a community translate emerging natural-resource opportunity into durable local prosperity?
How does a community translate education and human capital into durable local prosperity?

future_sie_synthesis.ask: Under what conditions did each development strategy succeed?
future_sie_synthesis.expected_insight: Some institutional designs may work across nearly all community types; others are highly context-dependent.

comparative_methodology.verdict_discipline: Reality—not preference—determines Supports / Qualifies / Contradicts for each hypothesis.

maturation_note.text: Ideas that once might have become doctrine now enter as research hypotheses, Living Community Laboratories, explicit questions, and predetermined Supports/Qualifies/Contradicts verdicts.
